title: True Negative
body:
Predicted negative, actually negative. A correct pass, and the cell of the [[Confusion Matrix]]
that is usually the biggest and least interesting.

It is the numerator of [[Specificity]], $\text{TN}/(\text{TN}+\text{FP})$: of the real negatives,
how many did you correctly leave alone.

**Its size is why accuracy lies.** On a rare-positive problem this cell dominates the table, so a
model that predicts negative every time scores well on
$(\text{TP}+\text{TN})/\text{total}$ while being useless. Neither [[Sensitivity]] nor precision
involves this cell at all, which is exactly why they are the metrics reported.

In [[STATISTICS]] this is correctly failing to reject a true $H_0$, at rate $1-\alpha$. See
[[Type I and Type II Errors]].
